research_notes: Blocked for the requested employment headlines: available dated roles are student/union/party or elected roles, all excluded by codebook. This does not establish zero other employment.

Checked official and party biographies, contemporary union inquiry material, ABC candidate history and targeted early-job/hospitality searches. No substantiated additional employer chronology emerged.
Any public/private total would require new evidence of non-excluded work with dates and full-time status; do not treat union representation of hospitality workers as hospitality employment.

Follow-up2026-10-02 overturns prior search gap: member’s2025 speech establishes previously omitted family-business assistance and casual bar employment during university. No calendar dates inferred from age14 years9 months. Whether the first formal job was the university bar role is not established; no extra duplicate role invented.

Targeted early-job/Hansard/own biography and employer-profile searches:2013 first speech and some2025 proceedings contain other members’ careers, which were not attributed to Chesters. Endometriosis ambassador image alt text belongs to another person and was ignored.

Next evidence: names/dates of family businesses and bar, nature of family remuneration, actual weekly hours, university dates/overlaps and dismissal date. Casual employment and union work do not become full-time public/private years. No gated-profile collection or outreach.

Third follow-up3October2026: a2014 first-person parliamentary speech locates the parents' second-hand furniture business on the Sunshine Coast and describes her working there for many childhood summers. This materially clarifies employer context and repeated seasonal work but supplies no legal name, calendar years, ordinary wage or hours; it is not converted to continuous employment. Searches did not identify the holiday-hire company or university bar. No headline totals changed.

Fourth follow-up4October2026: a2015 first-person House speech resolves the family furniture business name as CJ Discount Furniture and states that it had one award-paid employee while her parents did most work. The paid employee is not identified as Chesters; her separate2025 account describes pocket money for family-business tasks. The source materially improves employer identity but does not justify treating her as the award-paid worker, calculating a continuous seasonal interval or inferring hours. Holiday-hire business and university bar names/dates remain unresolved.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Added previously unrecorded UQ BA study from official parliamentary biography index. No study dates recovered. Exact-name bar, CJ Discount Furniture and holiday-hire searches returned known speeches only; UQ student-union operation of a campus bar does not prove it was her bar employer. Full-time disability/early-learning hits concern constituents or represented workers, not her personal employment. APH direct biography restricted; indexed qualification available. Next business/legal payroll identity, actual paid family role and casual bar dates/hours.

Fifth follow-up 5 October 2026: targeted family-business, university bar and early union searches in both engines found no original employer/payroll record for the casual bar role or individual holiday-hire terms. Her 2014 organiser speech confirms previously documented United Voice work, but its full-time cleaner examples refer to represented workers, not her own hours. The 2012 insecure-work inquiry witness list reiterates organiser presence within the supported union envelope. Derivative WhoRunsAus 1 January boundaries were rejected as invented precision for official year-only dates. Family award-paid employee remains unidentified; no assignment to Chesters. Further general searches exhausted. Next useful evidence is an original public personal CV or legitimate business/payroll history identifying the bar, hire employer, seasonal paid terms and exact intervals. No headline change.

Second targeted primary pass5October2026: recovered omitted first-person17July2014 account of16jobs across an approaching20year workforce history,mostly school/university-era casual work. Added nonadditive residual early-employment placeholder documenting that existing family-business/bar examples are not a complete chronology.16 is not treated as16 extra employers; collective casual earnings at full-time level do not prove any substantive FT appointment or support sector allocation. No dates calculated from age or anniversary. Targeted CJ Discount Furniture/hire-company searches yielded unrelated overseas furniture and logistics results, not personal employer identity. Both primary family-business facts and cash-paid bar role preserved. Next seek job-by-job public CV or original payroll records for unnamed early casual roles, employers,hours and overlaps. No headline total calculable.
